But since they ordered this bodily punishment to the salvation of the soul, it is added: [[5:5|that the spirit may be saved|ut spiritus salvus sit]], that is, that his soul may be saved, [[5:5|in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ|in die adventus Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], the day of the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, that is, the day of the general judgment, or of the particular judgment, that is, the day of death: which comes to the same thing. For as each one dies, so he will be presented to God on the day of judgment.

paras.t: Ex prædictis concludit Apostolus : Non est bona gloriatio vestra, o Corinthii, qua vel de baptistis et ministris gloriando contenditis, mutuoque præfertis, et ex hoc fraternam correctionem negligitis. Vel, gloriatio qua vos justos jactatis, bona non est, eo quod tantum peccatum inter vos toleretis. Qui enim non corrigit, quum potest et debet, communicat delinquenti, et particeps est peccati. Consequenter ostendit, quam periculosum sit congregationi sustinere perversum. Nescitis quia modicum fermentum, id est parva pars infectiva, totam massam corrumpit, id est, universam materiam inficit ? Sic unum peccatum, seu unus pestilens et perversus, videlicet consensus hujus peccati, et fornicator hujusmodi, totam massam, id est vestram congregationem, contaminat, inficit et seducit, nisi auferatur tale fermentum. Expurgate ergo vetus fermentum, id est, consensum peccati istius et auctorem peccati hujus amovete a vestra communione, ut sitis nova conspersio, id est gratia Baptismatis et virtutum operibus innovati, sicut estis azymi, id est a peccati fermento alieni effecti in fonte Baptismi. Azyma dicitur ab ἀ, quod est sine, et ζύμη, quod est fermentum, quasi sine fermento. Conspersio autem et azyma idem sunt, utpote farina per aquam glutinata sine fermento, sicque significant puritatem a corruptione peccati. Denique in fermento duo pensantur, videlicet : sapor virtualis, quo efficit panem saporosum ; et ita per fermentum signatur doctrina evangelica, ibi quum dicitur : Simile est regnum cælorum fermento, quod acceptum mulier abscondit in farinæ satis tribus, donec fermentatum est totum. Secundo consideratur in fermento corruptio adipis ; et ita significat culpam, quæ alios inficiendo corrumpit : et ita nunc sumitur.
paras.en: From what has been said the Apostle concludes: [[5:6|Your glorying is not good|Non est bona gloriatio vestra]], O Corinthians, by which you contend in glorying about your baptizers and ministers and set them above one another, and for this neglect fraternal correction. Or, the glorying by which you boast that you are just is not good, since you tolerate so great a sin among you. For one who does not correct when he can and ought, shares with the offender and is a partaker of the sin. Next he shows how dangerous it is for a community to tolerate a perverse man. [[5:6|Know you not that a little leaven|Nescitis quia modicum fermentum]], that is, a small infecting part, [[5:6|corrupteth the whole lump|totam massam corrumpit]], that is, infects the whole material? So one sin, or one pestilent and perverse man, namely consent to this sin and such a fornicator, contaminates, infects and leads astray the whole lump, that is, your community, unless such leaven is removed. [[5:7|Purge out the old leaven|Expurgate ergo vetus fermentum]], that is, remove consent to this sin and the author of this sin from your communion, [[5:7|that you may be a new paste|ut sitis nova conspersio]], that is, renewed by the grace of Baptism and the works of the virtues, [[5:7|as you are unleavened|sicut estis azymi]], that is, made strangers to the leaven of sin in the font of Baptism. *Azyma* comes from *a*, which means "without", and *zyme*, which is leaven: as it were "without leaven". *Conspersio* [paste] and *azyma* are the same, namely flour bound with water without leaven, and so they signify purity from the corruption of sin. Lastly, two things are considered in leaven: its strong savour, by which it makes bread tasty, and so leaven signifies the teaching of the Gospel, where it is said: [[Matt 13:33|The kingdom of heaven is like to leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until the whole was leavened|Simile est regnum cælorum fermento, quod acceptum mulier abscondit in farinæ satis tribus, donec fermentatum est totum]]. Secondly, the corruption of leaven is considered [the transcription reads *adipis*]; and so it signifies guilt, which corrupts others by infecting them: and it is taken so here.

paras.t: Sitis itaque nova conspersio : Etenim pascha nostrum immolatus est Christus, id est, agnus paschalis pro nostra salute oblatus est Christus : qui loquitur, Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam. De quo ait Joannes : Ecce Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi. Itemque alibi : Dignus est Agnus qui occisus est. Ipse enim verus est agnus qui abstulit peccata mundi, qui mortem nostram sui ipsius oblatione seu morte destruxit. Ipse quoque est pascha nostrum, id est transitus noster, præbendo nobis exemplum transeundi de hac peregrinatione ad patriam. Propter quod ait : Ego sum via, veritas et vita. Pascha enim transitus dicitur. Hujus Agni figura fuit agnus ille paschalis seu legalis, de quo in Exodo legitur. Unde quod ibi habebatur, Os ejus non confringetis, ab Evangelista allegatur de Christo. Similiter, sicut per effusionem sanguinis agni illius liberabantur filii Israel ab angelo devastante, seu plaga Ægypti, sic nos per effusionem sanguinis Christi liberamur a potestate diaboli et a ruina peccati. Insuper, sicut carnes agni illius manducabantur cum azymis panibus, sic fideles vivere et Christi corpus comedere debent sine fermento peccati. Ideo subditur :
paras.en: So be a new paste: [[5:7|For Christ our pasch is sacrificed|Etenim pascha nostrum immolatus est Christus]], that is, Christ has been offered as the paschal lamb for our salvation: who says, [[Jer 11:19|I was as a meek lamb, that is carried to be a victim|Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam]]. Of whom John says: [[John 1:29|Behold the Lamb of God. Behold him who taketh away the sin of the world|Ecce Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi]]. And likewise elsewhere: [[Apoc 5:12|The Lamb that was slain is worthy|Dignus est Agnus qui occisus est]]. For He is the true lamb who took away the sins of the world, who destroyed our death by the offering of Himself, that is, by His death. He is also our pasch, that is, our passage, giving us the example of passing over from this pilgrimage to the fatherland. For this reason He says: [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life|Ego sum via, veritas et vita]]. For pasch means passage[[Ex 12:11||]]. The figure of this Lamb was that paschal or legal lamb of which we read in Exodus. So what was said there, [[Ex 12:46|neither shall you break a bone thereof|Os ejus non confringetis]], is cited by the Evangelist of Christ[[John 19:36||]]. Likewise, just as by the shedding of that lamb's blood the children of Israel were set free from the destroying angel, or the plague of Egypt[[Ex 12:22||]][[Ex 12:23||]], so by the shedding of Christ's blood we are set free from the power of the devil and the ruin of sin. Moreover, as the flesh of that lamb was eaten with unleavened bread[[Ex 12:8||]], so the faithful should live and eat the body of Christ without the leaven of sin. So it is added:

paras.t: Itaque epulemur, id est, in Domino deliciemur ac nutriamur, Christi sacramentis vescamur, et ei incorporemur, non in fermento veteri, id est non in iniquitatibus nostris antiquis ac solitis, neque in fermento malitiæ, id est peccato ex deliberatione animi facto (juxta illud : Dixit injustus ut delinquat in semetipso), et nequitiæ, id est non in fraudulenta aliisque nociva conversatione, prout Petrus monet : Deponentes omnem malitiam et dolum et simulationes et invidias ; sed in azymis, id est operibus, sinceritatis, id est internæ puritatis, ut habeamus cor mundum, et veritatis, id est justitiæ, etiam quantum ad proximos ; vel, In azymis veritatis, id est actibus sanctæ contemplationis et illuminatæ cognitionis.
paras.en: [[5:8|Therefore, let us feast|Itaque epulemur]], that is, let us delight and be nourished in the Lord, feed on the sacraments of Christ and be incorporated into Him, [[5:8|not with the old leaven|non in fermento veteri]], that is, not in our old and customary iniquities, [[5:8|nor with the leaven of malice|neque in fermento malitiæ]], that is, sin done with deliberation of mind (according to the words: [[Ps 35:2|The unjust hath said within himself, that he would sin|Dixit injustus ut delinquat in semetipso]]), [[5:8|and wickedness|et nequitiæ]], that is, not in a deceitful conduct harmful to others, as Peter warns: [[1 Pet 2:1|laying away all malice and all guile and dissimulations and envies|Deponentes omnem malitiam et dolum et simulationes et invidias]]; [[5:8|but with the unleavened bread|sed in azymis]], that is, the works, [[5:8|of sincerity|sinceritatis]], that is, of inward purity, so that we may have a clean heart, [[5:8|and truth|et veritatis]], that is, of justice, also towards our neighbours; or, in the unleavened bread of truth, that is, in the acts of holy contemplation and enlightened knowledge.

paras.t: Scripsi vobis in epistola. Sciendum quod Apostolus, ante missionem præsentis epistolæ, misit Corinthiis epistolam quamdam, quæ non habetur : in qua jussit ut non miscerentur fornicariis, quod Corinthii non bene intellexerunt, putantes Apostolum loqui de spirituali fornicatione, quæ est idololatria. Ideo nunc exponit verba illic scripta, et ait : Scripsi vobis in epistola (illa quam non habemus), ne commisceamini fornicariis familiaritate, communione, aut cohabitatione : et non utique fornicariis hujus mundi, id est, hoc scripsi, ut non misceamini fornicariis hujus mundi, id est publice criminosis : de quibus subjungitur, aut avaris, aut rapacibus, id est violentis ablatoribus rei alienæ, aut idolis servientibus, id est idololatris, qui tamen Christiani esse volunt. Alioqui debueratis de hoc mundo exisse, id est, si aliter intellexissem quam sic, oporteret vos mundum omnino exire, si velletis mihi acquiescere. Nam si de gentilibus locutus fuissem, non possetis verba mea implere, nisi mundum exeundo, quum ubique demorentur gentiles. Nunc autem scripsi vobis in ista epistola clarius, non commisceri prædictis criminosis Christianis. De infidelibus namque non loquor : quibus etiam quomodo verbum salutis annuntiaretur, si vitarentur? Ideo additur : Si is qui frater, id est, si Christianus, nominatur inter vos fornicator, id est, notorius fornicator fuerit et convictus, aut avarus, aliena tenendo, aut idolis serviens, aut maledicus, id est detractor vel blasphemus, aut ebriosus, aut rapax, vel simili crimine vitiatus, cum hujusmodi nec cibum sumere, sed eum in omnibus evitare, ut erubescendo pœniteat. Unde alibi dicit Apostolus : Subtrahatis vos ab omni fratre ambulante inordinate. Non ergo prohibet cum infidelibus atque gentilibus sumere cibum, præsertim quum alias asserat : Si quis vocat vos infidelium ad cenam, et vultis ire, omne quod vobis apponitur manducate.
paras.en: [[5:9|I wrote to you in an epistle|Scripsi vobis in epistola]]. It must be known that the Apostle, before sending the present epistle, sent the Corinthians a certain epistle which we do not have, in which he commanded that they should not mix with fornicators. The Corinthians did not understand this well, thinking that the Apostle spoke of spiritual fornication, which is idolatry. So he now explains the words written there, and says: I wrote to you in an epistle (that one which we do not have), [[5:9|not to keep company with fornicators|ne commisceamini fornicariis]], by familiarity, communion or living together: [[5:10|I mean not with the fornicators of this world|et non utique fornicariis hujus mundi]], that is, I wrote this, that you should not mix with the fornicators of this world, that is, with public criminals: of whom it is added, [[5:10|or with the covetous or the extortioners|aut avaris, aut rapacibus]], that is, those who violently take away what belongs to others, [[5:10|or the servers of idols|aut idolis servientibus]], that is, idolaters, who yet want to be Christians [Denis takes "the fornicators of this world" as Christians who are public sinners]. [[5:10|otherwise you must needs go out of this world|Alioqui debueratis de hoc mundo exisse]], that is, if I had meant it otherwise, you would have to leave the world altogether if you wished to obey me. For if I had spoken of the Gentiles, you could not fulfil my words except by leaving the world, since the Gentiles live everywhere. [[5:11|But now I have written to you, not to keep company|Nunc autem scripsi vobis non commisceri]]: I have written to you more clearly in this epistle, not to keep company with the criminal Christians mentioned. For I do not speak of unbelievers: how would the word of salvation be preached to them if they were shunned? So it is added: [[5:11|if any man that is named a brother be a fornicator|Si is qui frater, id est, si Christianus, nominatur inter vos fornicator]]: a brother, that is, a Christian, a fornicator, that is, if he is a notorious and convicted fornicator, [[5:11|or covetous|aut avarus]], keeping what belongs to others, [[5:11|or a server of idols or a railer|aut idolis serviens, aut maledicus]], that is, a detractor or blasphemer, [[5:11|or a drunkard or an extortioner|aut ebriosus, aut rapax]], or stained by a like crime: [[5:11|with such a one, not so much as to eat|cum hujusmodi nec cibum sumere]], but to shun him in all things, so that he may be ashamed and repent. So the Apostle says elsewhere: [[2 Thess 3:6|that you withdraw yourselves from every brother walking disorderly|Subtrahatis vos ab omni fratre ambulante inordinate]]. He does not forbid, then, eating with unbelievers and Gentiles, especially since he asserts elsewhere: [[1 Cor 10:27|If any of them that believe not, invite you, and you be willing to go: eat of any thing that is set before you|Si quis vocat vos infidelium ad cenam, et vultis ire, omne quod vobis apponitur manducate]].

paras.t: Deinceps ostendit Apostolus, quod de infidelibus non habet dare præceptum. Quid enim mihi de his qui foris sunt, id est, quid spectat ad me de infidelibus, qui extra Ecclesiam sunt nomine, numero et re, judicare, id est dare sententiam ut vitentur? Imo potius debet se fidelis illis pie applicare, ut convertantur. Nonne de his qui intus sunt, id est fidelibus, qui intra Ecclesiam sunt nomine vel merito, vos judicatis, et non de his qui foris sunt? quasi dicat : Si vos non judicatis de his qui foris sunt, ita nec ego. Non […] [au]ctoritatem habeo super eos. Nam [eos qui] foris sunt, id est infideles, Deus [judicabit] judicio damnationis, non discus[sionis] […] [se]u disceptationis. Sic enim judicati sunt, juxta illud : Qui non cre[dit, jam] judicatus est, quia non credit in [nomine] unigeniti Filii Dei. […] [Auferte] malum, id est prædictum for[nicatorem] … qui habet uxorem patris sui, [ex vobis] ipsis, id est ex vestra societate. … [Qui] tetigerit picem, inquinabitur. Et [in Deut]eronomio Dominus : Auferes, in[quit, m]alum de medio tui, ut ceteri ti[morem] habeant. Debemus etiam auferre [cogitatio]nes malas et omne peccatum de [cordibus] nostris, prout per Prophetam [Dominus] jubet : Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows that he has no command to give about unbelievers. [[5:12|For what have I to do to judge them that are without|Quid enim mihi de iis qui foris sunt, judicare?]]: that is, what concern is it of mine to judge, that is, to pass sentence that they be shunned, about unbelievers, who are outside the Church in name, number and fact? Rather the faithful man should apply himself to them in kindness, that they may be converted. [[5:12|Do not you judge them that are within|nonne de iis qui intus sunt, vos judicatis?]], that is, the faithful, who are within the Church in name or merit, and not those who are without? As if he said: if you do not judge those who are without, neither do I. [The beginnings of the following lines are lost in the transcription; the gaps are filled here from the sense, as far as they can be.] I have no authority over them. [[5:13|For them that are without, God will judge|Nam … foris sunt … Deus]]: those who are without, that is, unbelievers, God will judge with the judgment of condemnation, not of examination or discussion. For so they have been judged, according to the words: [[John 3:18|he that doth not believe is already judged: because he believeth not in the name of the only begotten Son of God|judicatus est, quia non credit in]]. […] [[5:13|Put away the evil one|malum]], that is, the fornicator already mentioned, … who has his father's wife, [[5:13|from among yourselves|ipsis]], that is, from your company. … [[Ecclus 13:1|He that toucheth pitch, shall be defiled|tetigerit picem, inquinabitur]][[Lev 20:11||]] [the margin here gives Levit. xx, 11]. And the Lord in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 19:19|thou shalt take away the evil out of the midst of thee|auferes malum de medio tui]], [[Deut 19:20|That others hearing may fear|ut ceteri timorem habeant]] [the margin gives Deut. xiii, 19, 20; the words are those of Deut 19:19–20]. We ought also to put away evil thoughts and every sin from our hearts, as the Lord commands through the Prophet: [[Is 1:16|take away the evil of your devices from my eyes|Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis]].
